subject: Console: short customer-facing data transfer summary (rewrite request)
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acmecorp.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acmecorp.com
Date: 2025-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick ask — 'Where your data goes' blurb for the Console

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the product demo yesterday — the Console UI looks great. One follow-up from our privacy team: can you provide a plain-language, short (1-2 sentence) explanation we can show to our internal users in the Console about cross-border transfers and subprocessors for the Hosted API?

Specifically they asked for:
- A concise sentence that explains whether data may leave the EEA and why (processing, caching, redundancy)
- Whether Redwood relies on SCCs / adequacy / other mechanisms
- A one-line pointer to the DPA or Data Processing Addendum (link would be ideal)

We're trying to include a small tooltip under the "Data Residency" section and a short FAQ entry. Can you send something that is customer-facing (no legalese) but accurate?

Attachment: screenshot of where the tooltip will live (noted as screenshot.png)

Appreciate it — Alice
Privacy Program, AcmeCorp

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
To: alice.chen@acmecorp.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-30T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 'Where your data goes' blurb for the Console

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear note and the screenshot. Looping in Kimberly (privacy lead) and Laura (content for Console copy).

High level plan:
- We can provide two short variants: a succinct tooltip (1 sentence) and a 1-paragraph FAQ entry that expands on mechanisms and options (SCCs, adequacy, Dedicated/Private).
- We'll include a linked callout to the DPA and to the Console "Hosting & Transfers" page.

Kimberly / Laura, can you draft both pieces and mark any legal-sensitive phrases? Alice asked to avoid heavy legalese — she wants something product-friendly for end users. Target: turnaround today if possible.

Diego
Senior Product Manager
Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, alice.chen@acmecorp.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-30T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed copy: tooltip + FAQ draft (console_snippet_v1.txt attached)

Hi all — attached is a short snippet and a slightly expanded FAQ. I kept the language plain and product-focused. Two variant options below; happy to tweak wording.

Tooltip (one line) — Option A:
"Your data may be processed or stored outside the EEA to provide and improve the service. See our DPA for details about transfer safeguards."

Tooltip (one line) — Option B (more explicit):
"To operate the service and provide low-latency access, Redwood may process or store data outside the EEA (we use transfer safeguards such as SCCs or other lawful mechanisms). See the DPA for full details."

FAQ (short paragraph):
"Why might my data leave the EEA?
We sometimes process or cache requests outside the EEA to route them to nearby servers for performance, for backup, and to maintain reliability. When data is transferred across borders, we rely on appropriate safeguards — for example, Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), adequacy decisions, or contractual protections in our DPA — to protect data. Customers on Dedicated or Private deployments can choose EU-only hosting where required. Read the full Data Processing Addendum for details and subprocessors."

Placement suggestion:
- Tooltip under the Data Residency setting in Console (visible on hover).
- FAQ linked from the same setting and from the onboarding modal.

I attached a plain-text file (console_snippet_v1.txt) with the snippets and a short suggested link label: "Data processing & transfers (DPA)" that should point to https://docs.redwood.com/dpa.

Laura Bennett
Content Lead, Redwood Console

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: alice.chen@acmecorp.com
Date: 2025-12-01T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed copy: tooltip + FAQ draft (legal check)

Thanks Laura — good, clear options. A couple of small legal edits to keep the wording accurate without overloading the customer:

- Prefer the phrase "processed or stored outside the EEA" over "transferred" in the tooltip (more accurate for caching/processing).
- Replace "we rely on appropriate safeguards" with "we rely on transfer safeguards such as SCCs, adequacy decisions, or contractual protections (see DPA)" so it's slightly more specific but still customer-friendly.
- Add one line in the FAQ clarifying that controller/processor roles and retention policies are in the DPA.

Also: Diego, please confirm whether we should mention that Dedicated/Private customers may be able to restrict processing to EU-only infrastructure in the tooltip (I recommend only mentioning this in the FAQ to keep the tooltip short).

I'll attach the DPA excerpt we've been referencing (DPA-reference-acmecorp.pdf) for Alice's team.

Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
